call_points.text: Q1 EBITDA margin 9.3%, up 90 bps, on operating leverage, better mix and Bengaluru GCC efficiencies.
FY27 operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Tax rate guided at 10-15% for FY27-FY28 on carried-forward losses, normalising to about 20% after.
Plans to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to support hyperscale programmes.
On hyperscaler capex moderation, management said it sees no slowdown and new projects being announced.
GCC in Bengaluru to grow from 600 to 1,000 people, supporting project management and back office.
Acquisitions of $200-250 million of revenue a year, funded by internal accruals and some debt.
Receivable days rose to 90 plus on a March-heavy Q4; management expects a return to 60-75 days.
US skilled-labour shortage is inflationary; management is hiring from trade schools to ease margin pressure.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Disputes are as under pertaining to AY 2002-03: • Whether transfer of Tata Fone Division by the Company to ITEL Industries Private Limited was not a slump sale. • Whether no capital gain was taxable from the above transfer. • Whether lease income is taxable as business income. • Whether onus to prove that write off of obsolete stock was not bonafide was on the revenue without appreciating that assessee had failed to discharge primary onus to prove genuineness of its claim. Income Tax Department has filed appeal in High Court against order passed in favour of the Company. Next hearing date before High Court is awaited.

Issues are as under pertaining to AY 2003-04: • Whether lease income is taxable as business income. • Whether onus to prove that write off of obsolete stock was not bonafide was on the revenue without appreciating that assessee had failed to discharge primary onus to prove genuineness. Income Tax Department has filed appeal in High Court against order passed in favour of the Company. Next hearing date before High Court is awaited.

Income Tax department has disallowed certain expense which are in nature of for AY 2010-11: 1. Provision of Expense , 2. Renovation Expense Capitalised and 3. Change in Revenue Recognition Policy (Unearned Revenue) 4. Bad debts Written off The Company has received notice from the Commissioner of Appeals. Since we had received favourable order in the past for AY 2005-06 to AY 2009-10 in relation to unearned revenue, we expect the a similiar order for AY 2010-11. We have submitted additional evidence before CIT (A). The CIT(A) has forwarded the submission to the Asseeeing Officer for passing the remand report. We have been following up with the Assessing Officer regarding the same. During the quarter, we received the remand report from the Assessing Officer regarding the unearned revenue issue, which is in favour of the Company. We are currently awaiting further communication or notice from the CIT(A).
tax_litigation.status: Matter was argued, CIT(A) has referred back the matter to AO for verification of claim w.r.t. bad debts writen off

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessing Officer has disallowed certain expense for AY 2017-18 as under: 1. Provision of Expense. 2. Capitalisation of Renovation Expense. Further, Assesssing Officer has restricted the allowance of change in revenue recognition to the extent of returned loss. Hearing date before CIT(A) is awaited.

guidance.statement: Organic revenue to grow at a 17% CAGR to ₹12,000 Cr by FY30
EBITDA margin goal of 10% overall, to be reached in FY27
Order backlog to reach $1.3-1.4 billion by March 2027
Acquisitions of $200-250 million of revenue a year, funded by internal accruals and some debt
TPS product business revenue to reach $200 million by FY30 from $90 million
FY27 revenue guided at ₹7,800-8,000 Cr, 23-27% growth
FY27 EBITDA guided at ₹725-750 Cr, 27-32% growth, margin 9.3-9.4%
FY27 PAT guided at ₹300-325 Cr, 38-50% growth
Order backlog to reach US$1.3-1.4 bn by March 31, 2027, 65-75% growth
FY27 order bookings of US$1.3-1.4 bn, 32-45% growth
Medium-term EBITDA margin at or above 10%
Tax rate of 10-15% for FY27 and FY28, normalising to about 20% after
Aspiration to reach ₹18,000 Cr (US$2 bn) revenue by FY30, ₹12,000 Cr organic and ₹6,000 Cr inorganic

industry: Information Technology > IT - Services > IT Enabled Services

operating_notes.text: Order backlog was $800 million at March 2026, up $300 million, with data centres 25% of it and average age 15-18 months.
India contributes 6-7% of revenue, about $50 million, and is targeted at 8-10% of the $2 billion plan.
Effective tax rate is about 10% on carried-forward US net operating losses, expected for about two more years before 18-20%.
Order backlog was about US$950 mn at end-Q1FY27, up 83% YoY, with data centre engagement tenure of 24-36 months.
Q1FY27 bookings were US$339 mn; FY27 bookings guided at US$1.3-1.4 bn.
Brazil acquisition 2S added about ₹60 Cr of Q1FY27 revenue (two months of consolidation) and about US$50 mn of annual revenue.
